documents.title: Horus Heresy Overview
documents.content: The Horus Heresy, sometimes referred to poetically as the 'Age of Darkness', was a galaxy-spanning civil war that consumed the worlds of Mankind for 9 Terran years. Its outbreak marked the end of the Emperor of Mankind's Great Crusade to reunite the scattered colony worlds of Humanity.

documents.title: The Emperor and Primarchs
documents.content: The Emperor of Mankind created the Primarchs as his genetic sons, twenty superhuman beings designed to lead his Space Marine Legions during the Great Crusade. Each Primarch was a master of warfare, strategy, and leadership.

documents.title: Causes of the Heresy
documents.content: The Heresy was caused by multiple factors: Horus' corruption by Chaos, the Emperor's secrecy about the Webway Project, perceived abandonment by the Emperor, and manipulation by the Ruinous Powers of Chaos.

documents.title: Traitor Legions - Sons of Horus
documents.content: The Sons of Horus, formerly the Luna Wolves, were the XVI Legion led by Warmaster Horus Lupercal. They were the first to fall to Chaos and led the rebellion against the Imperium.

documents.title: Traitor Legions - Word Bearers
documents.content: The Word Bearers Legion, led by Primarch Lorgar, were the first to fall to Chaos worship. They orchestrated the corruption of Horus and spread Chaos cults throughout the Imperium.

documents.title: Loyalist Legions - Ultramarines
documents.content: The Ultramarines, led by Roboute Guilliman, were the largest Legion and remained loyal to the Emperor. They defended the Imperium Secundus while Horus marched on Terra.

documents.title: Major Battles - Isstvan III
documents.content: The Isstvan III Atrocity was the first major battle of the Heresy, where loyalist elements within traitor Legions were purged through viral bombardment and ground assault.

documents.title: Major Battles - Isstvan V Dropsite Massacre
documents.content: The Dropsite Massacre at Isstvan V saw three loyalist Legions ambushed and decimated by traitor forces, including Iron Hands, Salamanders, and Raven Guard. This event shattered loyalist response capability.

documents.title: Siege of Terra Overview
documents.content: The Siege of Terra was the final and most devastating campaign of the Heresy, where Horus' forces assaulted the Emperor's Palace on Terra itself. The siege lasted for 55 days.

documents.title: Chaos Gods' Role
documents.content: The four Chaos Gods - Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Slaanesh - manipulated events to corrupt Horus and his brothers. Each god offered power in exchange for worship and service.

documents.title: Key Characters - Horus Lupercal
documents.content: Horus Lupercal, Warmaster and Primarch of the Sons of Horus, was the Emperor's most beloved son who fell to Chaos corruption on Davin. He led the rebellion until his death aboard his flagship.

documents.title: Key Characters - Sanguinius
documents.content: Sanguinius, the Angel, Primarch of the Blood Angels, remained loyal to the Emperor and died defending the Imperial Palace. His sacrifice allowed the Emperor to confront Horus.

documents.title: Aftermath and Legacy
documents.content: The Heresy's aftermath saw the Emperor entombed on the Golden Throne, the Traitor Legions fled to the Eye of Terror, and the Imperium reorganized under the Codex Astartes.

documents.title: Timeline of the Heresy
documents.content: The Heresy spanned approximately 9 years, from Horus' wounding on Davin (005.M31) to his death aboard the Vengeful Spirit (014.M31). Each year saw escalating conflicts.

documents.title: Notable Quotes
documents.content: It was treachery at first. To turn against brothers, to kill for personal advancement and power. But we have seen them, how their minds and bodies have been corrupted. This is no longer Horus's treachery. It is his heresy.

documents.title: Space Marine Legions - Organization
documents.content: The original 20 Space Marine Legions were organized into companies and chapters, each numbering tens of thousands of warriors. Nine Legions turned traitor, nine remained loyal.

documents.title: The Great Crusade
documents.content: The Great Crusade was the Emperor's 200-year campaign to reunite humanity across the galaxy. It preceded the Heresy and set the stage for the conflict that would follow.

documents.title: Warmaster Horus - Rise to Power
documents.content: Horus earned the title of Warmaster through his unparalleled military victories and charismatic leadership. The Emperor appointed him supreme commander of all Imperial forces.

documents.title: The Emperor of Mankind
documents.content: The Emperor was an immortal perpetual who guided humanity's evolution. His vision was to create a secular, rational Imperium free from superstition and the influence of Chaos.

documents.title: Isstvan Massacres
documents.content: The Isstvan system saw two major betrayals: the viral bombing of Isstvan III and the Dropsite Massacre at Isstvan V. These events crippled loyalist response for years.

documents.title: Imperium Secundus
documents.content: Believing Terra had fallen, Roboute Guilliman established Imperium Secundus on Ultramar as a fallback government. Sanguinius was proclaimed Emperor regent.

documents.title: Mechanicum Schism
documents.content: The Mechanicum of Mars split during the Heresy, with Fabricator-General Kelbor-Hal leading the Dark Mechanicum in support of Horus while loyalist forges fought against them.

documents.title: Psychic Powers in the Heresy
documents.content: Psychic powers played a crucial role in the Heresy, from Magnus' warning to the corruption of Legions. The Council of Nikaea's edict against psykers was widely violated.

documents.title: Weapons and Warfare
documents.content: The Heresy saw the deployment of the most advanced weapons: Titans, power armor, plasma weaponry, and archaeotech. Both sides used virus bombs and orbital bombardment.

documents.title: Notable Heroes - Garviel Loken
documents.content: Captain Garviel Loken of the Sons of Horus remained loyal despite his Legion's fall. He became a founding member of the Knights-Errant, warriors who hunted traitors.

documents.title: Chaos Champions
documents.content: Chaos Champions like Abaddon, Khârn, Lucius, and Typhon rose to prominence during the Heresy, becoming legendary warlords who would terrorize the galaxy for millennia.

documents.title: Xenos Involvement
documents.content: While the Heresy was primarily human vs human, various xenos races were affected or involved: Eldar seers foresaw the conflict, Orks took advantage of the chaos, and Cabal attempted intervention.

documents.title: Imperial Army Forces
documents.content: The Imperial Army (later Imperial Guard) saw billions of soldiers fight on both sides. Entire regiments turned traitor while others remained fanatically loyal to the Emperor.

documents.title: Lost and Purged Legions
documents.content: Two Legions, the II and XI, were expunged from Imperial records before the Heresy. Their fate remains one of the great mysteries, though hints suggest catastrophic failures.

documents.title: The Ruinstorm
documents.content: The Ruinstorm was a massive warp storm created by the Isstvan massacres that cut off large portions of the galaxy, preventing loyalist forces from reaching Terra in time.

documents.title: Civil War Impact on Worlds
documents.content: Countless worlds were devastated during the Heresy. Some were virus-bombed, others saw brother fight brother, and many were lost to warp storms or daemonic incursions.

documents.title: Remembrancers
documents.content: Remembrancers were artists, poets, and historians who accompanied the Great Crusade to document humanity's expansion. Many witnessed the Heresy firsthand.

documents.title: Heresy Literature and Sources
documents.content: The Horus Heresy has been documented in dozens of novels, art books, and game supplements. The Black Library series spans over 50 books chronicling the conflict.

documents.title: Traitor Legion - Emperor's Children
documents.content: The Emperor's Children, led by Fulgrim, fell to Slaanesh through their pursuit of perfection. They became depraved warriors seeking only sensation and excess.

documents.title: Traitor Legion - Death Guard
documents.content: The Death Guard under Mortarion fell to Nurgle's plague. They became bloated, diseased warriors spreading contagion across the galaxy.

documents.title: Traitor Legion - World Eaters
documents.content: The World Eaters, led by Angron, were already brutal before Khorne's corruption. The Butcher's Nails implants drove them to berserker rage.

documents.title: Traitor Legion - Thousand Sons
documents.content: Magnus the Red's Thousand Sons fell through their quest for knowledge. The Rubric of Ahriman turned most into mindless automata.

documents.title: Loyalist Legion - Imperial Fists
documents.content: The Imperial Fists under Rogal Dorn were the Emperor's Praetorians, defending Terra and the Imperial Palace during the final siege.

documents.title: Loyalist Legion - Blood Angels
documents.content: The Blood Angels, led by Sanguinius, fought heroically throughout the Heresy. Their Primarch's death fighting Horus haunts them to this day.

documents.title: Final Battle - Emperor vs Horus
documents.content: The final confrontation between the Emperor and Horus aboard the Vengeful Spirit ended with Horus' death and the Emperor's mortal wounding. Sanguinius' sacrifice allowed this confrontation.
